items.cite: Beth L. Glixon, “Strozzi, Barbara”, *Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani*, vol. 94 (Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana, 2019).
items.note: An archival biography in Italian by the scholar who found many of the records, establishing dates, documents and dedications, with a bibliography.

items.cite: Ellen Rosand, “Barbara Strozzi, ‘virtuosissima cantatrice’: The Composer’s Voice”, *Journal of the American Musicological Society* 31/2 (1978), pp. 241–281.
items.note: A study of her career and style that relates her life, the Unisoni and the satires written against them to her arias and cantatas. Later accounts draw on it.

items.cite: Beth L. Glixon, “New Light on the Life and Career of Barbara Strozzi”, *The Musical Quarterly* 81/2 (1997), pp. 311–335.
items.note: Archival findings on her children, her loans and her finances, and on the letters of 1655 and 1665 that bear on her last books.

items.cite: Beth L. Glixon and Wendy Heller, eds., *Barbara Strozzi in Context* (Cambridge University Press, 2026).
items.note: On family, sex and the position of women in seventeenth-century Venice, and how they bore on her career. The essays include chapters on Giulio Strozzi and on Barbara as daughter and mother.

items.cite: Susan Clermont, “Barbara Strozzi at 400”, *In The Muse* (Library of Congress, 17 September 2019).
items.note: A short account of the Library of Congress copy of Diporti di Euterpe, Op. 7, of its dedication to Sagredo, and of the motet Quis dabit mihi in Sacra corona.

items.cite: Mario Ruffini, “Barbara Strozzi nel Novecento: la scoperta di una nuova composizione per il catalogo di Luigi Dallapiccola” (Centro Studi Luigi Dallapiccola, 2005), pp. 216–227.
items.note: On when, and by whom, Amor dormiglione was orchestrated. Documents the 1940 concert and Dallapiccola’s lost score, with a summary of her life and a bibliography.
